key_insight: MAGIC learns collaboration topologies by choosing the right granularity per role—single agent or reusable group—so one organization can mix fine-grained control with efficient shared patterns.
engineering_relevance: For multi-agent LLM systems, this enables task-specific graph design that can improve quality while reducing execution cost and improving reuse across subtasks.
method: Sequentially builds a mixed-granularity agent graph by selecting a functional role, instantiating it as an agent or group, then connecting it to existing units.
Uses dense-reward reinforcement learning with returns from current-policy trajectories to optimize graph construction.
Adds potential-based reward shaping from probe-based utility and structural signals to supply intermediate feedback without changing the overall task reward.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports outperforming state-of-the-art baselines across eight benchmarks and shows strong inference efficiency in an efficiency study.
watch_item: Training may be sensitive to reward shaping and probe design, since the method searches a combinatorial construction space with limited intermediate feedback.
paper_title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning
